title: Mothman
description: In 1966, people in Point Pleasant, West Virginia, reported seeing a mysterious winged creature with glowing red eyes.

title: Jackalope
description: The jackalope is a famous tall tale of the American West about a rabbit sporting the antlers of a deer.

title: Loveland Frogman
description: According to Ohio folklore, a strange human-sized frog has been spotted near the town of Loveland.

title: Squonk
description: Pennsylvania lumberjack folklore tells of a creature so unhappy with its appearance that it can dissolve into a puddle of tears.

title: Krampus
description: In Alpine Christmas folklore, Krampus accompanies Saint Nicholas and is said to visit misbehaving children on the night of December 5.

title: Fresno Nightcrawler
description: The Fresno Nightcrawler became an internet mystery after grainy footage appeared to show a pale creature made almost entirely of two walking legs.

title: Hodag
description: The horned Hodag of Rhinelander, Wisconsin, became famous through a clever monster hoax in the 1890s.

title: Champ
description: For generations, people have told stories about a mysterious lake monster named Champ lurking beneath Lake Champlain.

title: Jersey Devil
description: New Jersey folklore tells of a strange winged creature with hooves that haunts the Pine Barrens.

title: Flatwoods Monster
description: In 1952, a group in Flatwoods, West Virginia, reported encountering a towering creature with glowing eyes and an unusual pointed hood.

title: Ozark Howler
description: The Ozark Howler is said to roam the Ozark wilderness with shaggy dark fur, horns and a frightening howl.

title: Thunderbird
description: In the traditions of various Indigenous peoples of North America, the Thunderbird is a powerful supernatural bird associated with thunder and storms.

title: Dogman
description: Michigan folklore tells of a mysterious creature that looks like a dog but walks upright like a person.

title: Batsquatch
description: Pacific Northwest legends describe Batsquatch as a large ape-like creature with enormous bat wings.

title: Chupacabra
description: Stories of the chupacabra became famous in Puerto Rico in 1995, when a mysterious creature was blamed for attacks on farm animals.

title: Horned Bat
description: This imaginary Christmas creature combines the wings of a bat, the feet of a bird and a magical horn.

title: Nessie
description: The Loch Ness Monster is a legendary creature said to inhabit the deep waters of Scotland’s Loch Ness.

title: Werewolf
description: European folklore tells of people who can transform into wolves, often under the light of a full moon in modern stories.

title: Cthulhu
description: Cthulhu is a tentacled monster invented by author H. P. Lovecraft for a story published in 1928.

title: Wendigo
description: In some Algonquian-speaking Indigenous traditions, the Wendigo is a frightening supernatural being associated with hunger, greed and the dangers of winter.

title: Snallygaster
description: Maryland folklore describes the Snallygaster as a bizarre flying monster with features of both a bird and a reptile.

title: Yeti
description: Legends from the Himalayan mountains tell of a mysterious ape-like creature sometimes called the Abominable Snowman.

title: Belsnickel
description: In German and Pennsylvania Dutch Christmas traditions, Belsnickel is a fur-clad visitor who brings treats and tests whether children have behaved.

title: Mari Lwyd
description: In a Welsh winter tradition, a decorated horse skull is carried from house to house as people challenge one another in singing and rhyme.

title: Bigfoot
description: Bigfoot, also known as Sasquatch, is a legendary hairy giant said to leave enormous footprints in the forests of North America.
